correctness.rationale: Every selected set meeting both complete layers is connected iff it has at least one selected cross-matching edge, equivalent to A intersect B nonempty. Selection confined to one layer is not secure since an omitted opposite vertex has only its paired partner as defender and its swap destroys connectivity. If both layers have at least two selected vertices, for every outside u its same-layer defender can be chosen without removing the last selected matching bridge. A singleton layer is secure only when the other layer is full: otherwise swapping the sole selected singleton to an omitted same-layer index kills every selected bridge; if the opposite layer is full the swap to any outside same-layer vertex succeeds. All-set polynomial subtracts disjoint pairs of sizes >=2 and adds n singleton/full-layer patterns on each side; minimal four-sets count C(n,2)(2n-3), and singleton/full layers supply 2n more, with n=3 degree collision. Independently enumerated all 2^(2n) selections and all legal one-vertex defenders n=3..6 and recomputed minimality (22,123,636,3001 SCD sets). This supports but does not replace the uniform combinatorial proof.
residual_risks: Definition is single-vertex replacement preserving both connectedness and closed-neighborhood domination, not defensive alliance, eternal security or secure total domination.
n=3 minimality polynomial has both contributions at z^4; avoiding a false distinct-size assertion.

value.rationale: The family K_n□K2 is a canonical, connected, n-regular graph with a thin matching bridge between highly connected layers. Classifying every secure connected dominating set and all inclusion-minimal ones makes a natural replacement-security distinction exact; γ_sc=4 but maximal minimal cardinality n+1 gives an unbounded, mathematically motivated gap within a highly symmetric graph family. The enumerator contains more information than a textbook bound on domination number.
residual_risks: The proof uses elementary clique/matching case analysis; importance rests on the structural all-n characterization and minimality gap, not algorithmic complexity.

final_claim: For all n>=3, S subset K_n square K_2 is secure connected dominating iff layer index sets A,B share a matching index and either both have >=2 members, or one is singleton and other full. The bivariate SCD polynomial is the size>=2 independent-clique product minus disjoint A,B pairs plus n(xy^n+x^ny). Inclusion-minimal cardinality polynomial is C(n,2)(2n-3)z^4+2nz^(n+1), giving gamma_sc=4 and max minimal size n+1.
